facts.statement: The study focuses on human brain development, specifically tracing the origin of basal ganglia neurons to the ganglionic eminences in the prenatal brain.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Researchers used a combination of single-nucleus methyl-3C sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and single-molecule imaging to map how these brain structures develop.

facts.statement: Different subregions of the ganglionic eminences showed varied timing in their developmental progression.

facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: A specific, temporary chromatin state was observed during the development of oligodendrocytes in infancy, indicating that chromatin shapes linked to cell fate can be temporary.

facts.statement: The temporal part of the cortex showed faster epigenetic maturation compared to other areas of the cortex during the studied period.
